```plato

    //==
    // # Solver bodies — impulse response
    //
    // Everything the solver needs to know about one body, and the reason
    // `SolverBody3D` stores an inverse inertia DIAGONAL rather than a tensor:
    // applying I^-1 is then a rotation into the principal frame, three multiplies,
    // and a rotation back, with no matrix to assemble and nothing to invert.

    // The dimensionless mobility of a motion kind: 1 for a body that responds to
    // impulses, 0 for one that does not. The single place in this library that
    // reads `BodyMotion`, so that the solver itself has no case analysis and no
    // branch a static body can take by accident.
    MobilityScale(motion: BodyMotion): Number
        => match (motion) {
            Static => 0.0;
            Kinematic => 0.0;
            Dynamic => 1.0;
        };
```
